newsitem.title: GERMANY: Copper group KM Europa sees higher 97 sales.
newsitem.headline: Copper group KM Europa sees higher 97 sales.

text.p: KM Europa Metal group, the leading European copper processor, said it expects a modest rise in copper demand to contribute to higher earnings and profitability in 1997.
New orders for the conmpany's varied copper, brass and alloy products in first quarter 1997 were up 10 percent over the same 1996 period, board spokesman Norbert Brodersen told a news conference.
"We expect two or three percent growth in sales to our traditional European markets," he said. Sales might pick up more rapidly towards the end of the year and beyond.

Brodersen said further efforts would be made to strengthen the group's sales of industrial products such as brass bars and copper moulds in overseas countries outside Europe, which account for 10 percent of the sales total.
Demand for KME products in the U.S. was forecast to rise by four to five percent and in the Far East the rise was seen at between five and 10 percent.
Construction sector products, which account for 52 percent of total sales, were selling reasonably well, with the replacement sector livelier than new building activity.
Industrial products sales, which are less exposed to seasonal swings, would grow in line with overall trends.
Brodersen said pre-tax profits in 1997 might rise to 130 million marks after 119 million in 1996.
The improvement in 1996, from 100.1 million a year earlier, had not been achieved through profitable product sales, but reflected restructuring efforts.
The group's sales in 1996 fell to 3.80 billion marks from 3.98 billion in 1995, partly a result of lower copper prices.
Sales of KME's copper semi-fabricated products, sheet, bars, tubes and cables in 1996 were down at 720,000 tonnes from 800,000 in 1995.
KME was improving its value-added special products for industrial purposes such as superconductors, casting moulds, specially coated cables, as well as innovative tubes.
It was also hopeful to participate in massive and potentially lucrative projects to supply blanking coins for the Euro, the planned European currency.
KME, the result of an amalgamation of companies across Europe two years ago, operates 18 plants in four countries and accounts for 70 percent of European copper semis production.
It is part of the Italian SMI - Soc Metallurgica Italiana SpA group.
